catalog_quote: [Shimoji 2008: 81] Irabu lacks lexical prosody, or is an 'accentless' language (Hirayama 1964, 1967, Hirayama, Oshima, and Nakamoto 1966, Nakasone n.d (b). However, Irabu shows a strikingly rigid prosodic organisation in terms of rhythmic structure. Irabu prosody has a hierarchical structure in which the most basic structure is mora structure, which is the tone-bearing unit and which is in turn the basis of bi- or trimoraic foot structure based on which tone is assigned to produce rhythmic alternation of tones (High and toneless). ... [96-97] (2-67) Tone assignment rule a. Group one to three adjacent feet into a single 'foot group' ... c. Assign /H/ to the left-most foot of each foot group. ... [Hayashi 2010: 171] Ikema is a language with a word-tone system. Lexical tone appears at the right-most position of the lexical word. There are two patterns (α/β) in the system ... Just like the…

Deciding source is the Glottolog top-ranked reference grammar (Shimoji 2008 ANU PhD, 608 pp) by the principal fieldworker, with an explicit rule-based prosody chapter, plus two specialist sketches. sources.citation: Pellard, Thomas. 2009. Ōgami: Éléments de description d'un parler du Sud des Ryūkyū. Thèse de doctorat, EHESS, Paris (451 pp.). TEL tel-00444150
sources.quote: p.106: 'Comme dans l'ensemble des variétés de la famille japonique, il n'y a pas d'accent d'intensité, distinctif ou rythmique, dans le dialecte d'Ōgami. La fréquence fondamentale ne semble pas non plus jouer de rôle distinctif ... La quasi totalité des dialectes de Miyako semble avoir perdu son système tonal originel, qui ne subsiste aujourd'hui de manière avérée que dans les dialectes d'Ikema (Hayashi et al. 2008, 2009) et de Tarama Matsumori (2001).' p.107: same word in isolation varies freely in melody (Fig. 3.31, funi 'bateau').

sources.citation: Igarashi, Yosuke, Yukinori Takubo, Yuka Hayashi, Thomas Pellard and Tomoyuki Kubo. 2012. Ryūkyū Miyako-go Ikema hōgen no akusento taikei wa sankei de atte nikei de wa nai [The Ikema dialect of Miyako Ryukyuan has a three-, not two-, pattern accent system]. Onsei Kenkyū 16(1): 134-148. doi:10.24467/onseikenkyu.16.1_134 (HAL hal-01289283)
sources.quote: 'we test the hypothesis that Ikema, a dialect of Miyako Ryukyuan, has a three-pattern accent system, where three accent classes, Types A, B, and C, are lexically distinguished, contra previous studies which have claimed that it has a two-pattern accent system. The results of our analysis confirm the existence of three distinct accent classes.' Acoustic (F0) study; prosody treated entirely as lexical pitch classes, no stress.

sources.citation: Shimoji, Michinori. 2009. Foot and Rhythmic Structure in Irabu Ryukyuan. Gengo Kenkyu 135: 85-122. doi:10.11435/gengo.135.0_85
sources.quote: p.90: 'All previous works on Irabu prosody agree that Irabu is a language with no lexically contrastive prosodic patterns (Hirayama 1964, 1967; Hirayama, Oshima, and Nakamoto 1966; Shimoji 2007).' p.114: 'The differences are that in Irabu the marked prosodic feature is tone rather than stress and such a feature is borne by an entire foot rather than an individual syllable.' Abstract (p.85): Irabu prosody 'characterised by a foot-based alternating rhythm of tone features'.
